context:
Goal: builders and reviewers judge screens by one list of house rules.
Problem (rule): the house-rules record lists 14 ids and the design docs hold 34; your note settled most of them and asked about the rest.
Based on (ruling): 183 none (11:22 CST Nov 6). Asked again because your note asked for explanations of the rules below.
Based on (read): docs/decisions/ux-house-rules.md lists 14; docs/design/principles.md and layout.md hold 34.
Departs from: ux-house-rules.md, which lists 14 house rules — your ticks plus the settled list below set the new list.

Settled by your note (a lane writes it once this item is answered):
- House rules: the first 13 the record lists; ux-unknown-is-not-empty, with ux-empty-one-action folded into it; ux-haptics-feel-substantial; ux-gap-on-parent.
- Not house rules, kept in the design docs as guidance ("skip"): ux-order-holds-still, ux-statements-are-true, ux-no-dead-end.
- Removed from the design docs too: ux-ask-or-undo ("disagree as a guideline even anywhere").
- ux-swift-same-intent: a lane checks whether it holds (roadmap step ux-swift-same-intent-check).
If I read "skip" or ux-ask-or-undo wrong, say so in the note.

Tick each rule below that should be a house rule. An unticked rule stays in the design docs as guidance only.
- ux-feature-baseline-or-fallback: a page uses a new browser feature (such as a CSS trick only the newest Chrome has) only after it checks the browser has it, and else shows a plain version that still works. It stops a blank or broken screen on an older phone.
- ux-press-moves-nothing: a press or a load never shoves other things on the screen (a banner appears and the button you were about to tap jumps down). From banchi D118 and D313.
- ux-keep-what-was-made, softened: typed input that no server can bring back survives leaving and coming back. "Never" is dropped. From q_max D-399.
- ux-machine-text-hidden: error codes, file paths and record ids sit behind a closed "Details", so the screen speaks plainly. From banchi D196 and D269.
- ux-control-earns-place: a button or filter that would do nothing on this screen is not shown, and an expected one that is off says why ("Export: no rows yet"). From q_max D-675.
- ux-one-plain-name: the menu label is the page title, an act such as "Archive" has the same name on every screen, and an icon means one thing. From q_max D-582.
- ux-a11y-floor: each screen passes the basics in a11y.md: readable contrast, labels a screen reader reads, keyboard use, tap size. Who made it: built from q_max D-648 (contrast floor) and banchi's automatic accessibility test (axe on its component gallery).
- ux-layout-primitives: pages are built from a few named blocks (a stack, a row, a grid, a sidebar), each owning its own spacing, not one-off spacing on each page.
- ux-control-beside-area: tabs, a filter or a toggle sit right next to the list or panel they change, with nothing between.
- ux-component-reads-its-box: a shared piece, such as a card, picks its narrow or wide shape from the space it is given, not from the window size. Near ux-gap-on-parent: that one says who sets the spacing; this one says who picks the shape.
- ux-variant-extends-home: when a screen needs a slightly different card, the shared card gets an option; nobody copies it. Your home repo's "shared screens" rule says the same for views.
- ux-fluid-tokens: sizes that grow with the space (a heading that scales with the box) come from named shared values, not numbers typed in each file. Yes, near ux-gap-on-parent: both keep layout values in one place.

lastAnswer.note: Owner asked what is lost without b (a press moves nothing). Routed the picks 13:16 CST to the coordinator; b answered in the reply.

title: Which of these 12 UX rules should also be house rules?
why: Recommended: the first three. Each stops a harm a person feels (a broken screen, a mis-tap, lost typing). The rest stay as guidance until a screen shows the harm.
